common: Complete the maintenance task while preserving existing behavior supported by evidence. Check startup, admission, completion, cancellation, and ownership of side effects separately.

by_label.R: Identify the actual readiness conditions and inspect execution paths before they are met, while waiting, and after resumption. Determine when execution may continue from the current task, rather than inferring policy from field names such as ready or loading.
by_label.O: Inspect listener registration, state publication, and external callbacks in actual call order. When synchronous callbacks can reenter, check whether the state and request remain valid after the callback returns. Resolve priorities according to the current task.
by_label.B: Check whether submission, persistence, or cleanup obligations must be completed before a return, handoff, or dependent effect. Examine flushing, waiting, and cancellation separately; do not treat every asynchronous operation as a completion barrier.
by_label.L: Identify the lifetimes governing work admission, resource cleanup, and side effects separately. Inspect inputs and callbacks before and after closing, switching, or cancellation. Stopping new input does not automatically revoke all previously admitted work.
by_label.I: Trace ownership of requests, visits, documents, and data snapshots at entry, reentry, and completion. Inspect persistent results and UI feedback separately; current evidence must establish whether the entry identity should be retained.
by_label.F: Within the same logical owner, inspect competition between result arrival order, completion order, and edit revisions. Verify both in-order and reverse-order completion. Distinguish owner invalidation from revision freshness within a retained owner.
by_label.A: Use current requirements to establish which admitted work must be retained, discarded, or deduplicated, and how many times effects may occur. Check whether consumption records and individual attempts have different lifetimes, and verify that the repair preserves existing retention behavior.
